intro.title: House Robber II
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a solution to the House Robber II problem, where you need to maximize the amount of money a robber can steal from houses arranged in a circle without triggering adjacent alarms. You'll learn how to apply dynamic programming concepts to break down this circular problem into two linear subproblems. The implementation will involve using JavaScript arrays, loops, and helper functions to calculate optimal results. By the end, you'll understand how to handle circular constraints by solving simpler linear cases and combining their results.
intro.usecase: The House Robber II algorithm pattern appears in resource allocation systems where you need to maximize value while respecting constraints on adjacent selections. In finance dashboards, this helps optimize investment portfolios by selecting non-adjacent high-yield assets while avoiding risk clusters. E-commerce platforms use similar logic for dynamic pricing engines to maximize revenue without discounting adjacent product categories. This circular constraint pattern also appears in scheduling systems for optimizing shift assignments or equipment maintenance rotations in manufacturing interfaces.
